title: Auto directionality of slot behaves different than for other elements
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The [auto-directionality](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#auto-directionality) algorithm differentiates between `dir=auto` slots, form elements and other elements. The special case for slot is necessary as we use the assigned nodes instead of descendants to determine the direction. The slot together with its assigned nodes forms a tree. I would assume the directionality should be computed from this tree as is done for the DOM subtree of any other `dir=auto` element. But there are some slight differences between the handling of slots and other elements.

I'm not sure if these differences are intended. Also, the directionality of a slot element with assigned nodes might not matter. The assigned nodes inherit their direction from the light tree and the slot is not visible.

### Examples 

- the input element value can impact the auto directionality of a slot
- the content of `bdi` elements impacts the auto directionality of a slot
- the dir attribute of assigned nodes is ignored, if a `dir=ltr` div with rtl text is assigned to the slot, the text can impact the auto directionality of that slot

While adding several directionality tests, I also included some test cases for those in [/html/dom/elements/global-attributes/dir-slots-directionality.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/4df85d1ac95ee7f6fb685055ba16ce91e5d0b876/html/dom/elements/global-attributes/dir-slots-directionality.html#L162-L226).

### Cause

The cause of these differences are
1. for slot, we do not skip `bdi`, `script`, `style`, `textarea`, and elements with valid `dir` as is done in [step 3.1](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#auto-directionality)
2. calling upon the auto-directionality of child in [step 2.1.3.2](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#auto-directionality) is not the same as walking the subtree and getting the directionality from text nodes, as the child might be an [auto-directionality form-associated element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#auto-directionality-form-associated-elements).

### Suggested solutions

An easy option would be to copy step 3.1 to before 2.1.1 followed by another check for auto-directionality form-associated input. We could also include input directly in step 3.1.

Alternatively, steps 2 and 3 can be unified by having an algorithm for determining the auto directionality from a tree.

@dbaron
